# MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1 Lubrication and fluids - Machining CNC turning center #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-CN02

## Scope
This maintenance manual specifies lubrication and fluid handling for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02). It defines required consumables, inspection points, refill routing, and recordkeeping for normal production operations. This document applies to maintenance technicians and machine operators responsible for preventive lubrication and fluid control during line P3-L3 production runs. Refer to SOP-P3-L3-01, SOP-P3-L3-03, and SOP-P3-L3-05 for complementary safe work and lockout procedures.

Background: Proper lubrication of slideways, ball screws, bearings, and tooling interfaces is essential to maintain machining accuracy, minimize wear, and prevent unplanned downtime. This document captures the method and rationale for lubrication frequency and fluid identification for EQ-P3-L3-CN02.

The way lube refill interval for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 70 hours.  
The lubricant part number for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is CFW-LUB-611.

## Tools and materials
- Approved lubricant: CFW-LUB-611 (as above). Use only this part for all factory-specified lubrication points on EQ-P3-L3-CN02.
- Clean dispensing pump with filter sock and tagged spout (dedicated to CFW-LUB-611).
- Lint-free rags and lint-free gloves.
- Fluid-level inspection mirror and flashlight.
- Absorbent pads and drip tray for spill control.
- Records logbook or tablet entry configured per local CMMS referencing MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1.
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P3-L3-01 and SOP-P3-L3-03.

Rationale for materials: A dedicated pump and filtered dispensing minimizes particulate contamination that accelerates wear and leads to premature failure. Using the exact lubricant part CFW-LUB-611 ensures consistent viscosity and additive performance across bearings and slides.

## Procedure
Overview: The procedure below provides step-by-step actions for safe, consistent lubrication of EQ-P3-L3-CN02 during scheduled maintenance windows and as required by production observations. Follow lockout/tagout instructions in SOP-P3-L3-05 when access to guarded components is required.

Pre-task
- Confirm machine status and notify production. Obtain permission to access machine work envelope.
- Review recent maintenance log entries for EQ-P3-L3-CN02 to identify any recurring issues.
- Verify availability of CFW-LUB-611 and that dispensing equipment is clean and properly labeled.

Inspection and preparation
- Visually inspect lubricant reservoirs and sight glasses for contamination, water ingress, and level indication.
- Where applicable, wipe sight glass and cap area to clean before opening filler ports.
- Place drip tray under access panels and have absorbent pads ready.

Dispensing and refill
- Use the dedicated pump to add CFW-LUB-611 to the designated refill ports. Fill only to the indicated level on the machine sight glass or reservoir mark.
- After refill, cycle affected axes through their full travel at low speed to distribute lubricant into circulation paths. Observe for any leaks or abnormal noises.
- If any contamination or emulsion is observed during the refill, stop the procedure, contain the fluid, and escalate to maintenance supervision per SOP-P3-L3-03.

Examples and special cases
- If machining cadence is increased or heavy cutting is observed, document the event and consider additional visual checks between scheduled refills. Record the reason for the additional check in the logbook.
- If an operator reports excessive axis friction or stick-slip, perform the inspection steps and confirm that CFW-LUB-611 was used in the last refill entry.

Rationale for procedure choices: Sight-glass leveling and cycling axes after adding lubricant ensures trapped air is released and lubricant reaches bearing interfaces. Using a dedicated pump prevents cross-contamination from other fluid types that are not compatible with CFW-LUB-611.

Records and documentation
- Log each refill and inspection entry in the EQ-P3-L3-CN02 maintenance log. Required entry fields: equipment id (EQ-P3-L3-CN02), technician name, lubricant part number (CFW-LUB-611), machine operating hours at time of refill, anomalies observed, and corrective actions taken.
- Attach any digital photos of contamination or abnormal wear to the CMMS work order and reference SOP-P3-L3-05 for corrective action steps.
- Retain spill reports and disposal records according to site environmental procedures referenced in SOP-P3-L3-01.

The way lube refill interval for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 70 hours. This interval is based on typical machine duty cycles and OEM lubricant life characteristics; deviations must be documented and justified in the maintenance log.

## Acceptance criteria
Lubrication outcome for EQ-P3-L3-CN02 is acceptable when all of the following are met:
- Reservoirs and sight glasses show correct level following refill and no visible contamination is present.
- Post-refill axis cycling shows smooth motion without abnormal vibration or noise.
- Maintenance log entries contain the required fields and explicitly list CFW-LUB-611 for the service event.
- No fluid leaks are observed in the immediate area and no evidence of cross-contamination is present.

Unacceptable conditions and corrective action
- Any sign of contamination, water intrusion, or incompatible fluid requires immediate containment, sampling, and replacement of contaminated fluid with CFW-LUB-611. Escalate per SOP-P3-L3-03.
- Missing or incomplete records trigger a follow-up audit and repeat of the refill procedure to confirm compliance.
- Repeated lubrication-related alarms or wear patterns should prompt a full lubrication system inspection and possible component replacement per SOP-P3-L3-05.

Notes on continuous improvement
- Track lubricant consumption and log trends against the scheduled 70 hours interval to identify potential leaks or increased consumption.
- Feedback from operators and technicians should be recorded and used to refine access, labeling, and dispenser maintenance to reduce contamination risk.

Related documents: SOP-P3-L3-01, SOP-P3-L3-03, SOP-P3-L3-05
